summary: Net positive, but not safe to stage unreviewed. Of 58 accepted rewrites, 33 improved, 17 neutral, and 8 harmful: 3 meaning-changed, 1 lost-context, 4 worse-readability, 0 slop. Autofixes are low risk (20 of 23 neutral), but dash-gloss turns 3 'Applies to' glosses into verbless fragments. Semicolon splits are the reliable win; dash-to-comma or colon swaps are compliance only. no-new-findings blocks clean prose splits (list-item-sentences, paragraph-length), so the strong model falls back to bullets with false hierarchy or bare colon swaps. Worst: sidecar-d puts sequence sidecars under assets/canvases/, the editing intro drops the save loop from its scope, and reconcile-gloss becomes a comma-spliced run-on; fact-check passed all three (0.27, 0.32, 0.11). All 4 rejections were correct. Fix first: skip dash-gloss when the gloss has no verb, exempt role lines, let splits raise sentence counts, require every structural target fixed, and send bulleted or scope-bearing rewrites to human review.

Page grows from 26 to 45 blocks. The 5-item list cap likely kept doc-schema.ts in the lead while its four peer modules became bullets.

b-ec-sidecar-d now claims sequence sidecars live under assets/canvases/; fact-check passed it at 0.27. Revert before staging.

The intro paragraph became a lead plus four bullets. The fast model's clean prose split was blocked by structure.opening-length and ste.paragraph-length.
Some Decision and Why items now nest sub-bullets while untouched siblings stay flat two-sentence items, so the page mixes two shapes.
Package role lines get invented verbs ('includes' here, 'defines one definition' in docs-model). Exempt role lines or give them an 'X is ...' template.
